hits.name: Rowan Cheung
hits.text:
I'm GrokBot pilled.

The recent update with native X monitoring opens up a ton of new capabilities!

My 4 favorite routines (copy/paste these prompts):

Routine 1: Find real AI workflows on X (and skip the hype threads)

Every morning, this bot now finds real AI use cases being shared on X, and filters out the “10 prompts” hype threads.

“Every weekday at 9:15am in my time zone, search X and the web for new AI workflows people are actually running. Keep only cases that name the old task, the tool, and the result: time saved, a step removed, or a handoff that used to need a person. Drop product announcements, “10 prompts” threads, and anything the author has not used more than once. Return at most 3. For each, give the link, the job it replaces, what I would need connected, and whether it fits my work. Send it to me on Slack. Do not post or reply anywhere else. Save this as a routine. If nothing qualifies, send one line saying so.”

Routine 2: Catch every mention of your brand

This bot catches every mention of The Rundown on X, labels it, and pings our team on Slack to respond (try tweeting us @therundownai and see what happens).

“Every weekday at 9:00am, search X for mentions in the last 24 hours of [your brand, @handle, or your own name]. For each hit, give the author, link, a one-line summary, and whether it is praise, complaint, question, or neutral. Do not reply to anyone. Post the digest in [your Slack channel] and tag me. Save this as a routine. If a source is unavailable, say which one.”

Routine 3: Find people actively looking for what you do

Every 4 hours, this bot listens for people searching for the best AI newsletter on X, so we know exactly what readers are looking for.

“Every 4 hours, search X for people evaluating [your category]. Catch three things: reviews or complaints about [category]; posts asking which [category] to use; and complaints about the problem [your product] solves. Quote the post, link it, name the account, and label it review, shopping, or complaint. Skip anything older than 24 hours, and skip [category] accounts promoting themselves. Post to [your Slack channel] only if there is at least one new hit you haven’t already shared. Do not reply to or interact with anyone. Save this as a routine. If the search fails, report the failure in Slack.”

Routine 4: Never lose a new contact again

I meet A LOT of people at events. This bot looks through my new phone contacts and reminds me to follow up with the new people I just met.

“Every weekday at 8:30am in my time zone, read my address book and list contacts added in the last 14 days. For each, show name, date added, phone, email, and any note. Ask me what we talked about before you write anything. Once I reply, draft a follow-up task for each person in [your task tool] with the context attached. Never text, email, or call anyone. Save this as a routine. If the address book is unavailable, say so and do not use old data.”
hits.hook: I'm GrokBot pilled.  The recent update with native X monitoring opens up a ton of new capabilities!  My 4 favorite routi
hits.quote_note: @bot: Grok Bot can now search, read, and monitor X. (5.14M)
hits.draft_en:
Rowan shared four Grok Bot routines he copy-pastes. 524k views. Look at how each one ends.

'Do not post or reply anywhere else.' 'Do not reply to anyone.' 'Never text, email, or call anyone.' 'If a source is unavailable, say which one.'

The trick is not the schedule. It is the guardrail line. Every routine says what the bot must never do and what to report when it fails.

Write one routine tonight with three parts: when it runs, what it returns, and one sentence of what it must never do.
hits.video_tip: 10s: a routine prompt typed out, with the 'never do' line highlighted in red, then a calm Slack digest arriving, caption every routine needs a never.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
I discovered that 1000s of bots are actively monitoring X for new links posted, probably not just on my account

I noticed when everytime I'd share one of my sites new features or pages, the page would get a bit slower just after posting, then I asked Claude to analyze it

I tweeted a test URL as a reply somewhere deeply hidden in a thread (so not even a main post)

And within 8 seconds there's thousands of crawlers opening the page!

One is a military intelligence firm, that scans social media for breaking news and sells alerts to newsrooms, banks, companies and government, it specifically follows accounts with many followers

Another one is a social media monitoring company that tracks what people say online

I knew of course high frequency trading firms use online news to trade fast on things, but interesting to see it in real life

Twitterbot (X) of course is first, within 0 seconds of sharing, it opens it (probably when I wrote the tweet)

The first non-X bot arrives just 8.40s later, which I think is pretty fast considering it's a reply by me deeply hidden in a thread somewhere

TL;DR they're watching you!
hits.hook: I discovered that 1000s of bots are actively monitoring X for new links posted, probably not just on my account  I notic
hits.draft_en:
Pieter posted a test link as a reply buried deep in a thread. X's own bot opened it instantly. The first outside crawler hit it 8.40 seconds later, then thousands more.

One was a military intelligence firm selling alerts to newsrooms, banks and governments. Another was a social monitoring company.

He only found out because his pages slowed down after every post, so he asked Claude to read the logs.

Your launch link gets read by machines before your first fan sees it.

Before your next launch post, cache the page, tail your logs for the first 60 seconds, and count who shows up.
hits.video_tip: 10s: terminal tail of access logs, quiet, then a post goes live and the screen floods with requests, timer stamped 8.40s, caption they read your links first.

hits.name: GREG ISENBERG
hits.text:
[X Article] Marketing Engineers: 100x More Experiments with AI agents

Marketing engineers are the new 10x employee, and most companies don't have one yet.
If you're growing a startup, a business or a side hustle, becoming one or hiring one is the biggest lever you have right now. It's the most exciting time to be in marketing since Google launched AdWords. Maybe ever.
For 20 years, marketing ideas were easy and shipping them was hard. Sales knew why deals closed. Support knew why customers left. But every idea had to survive a brief, a designer, a developer, an analyst and two meetings, and most died in a Slack thread.
That bottleneck just broke!
Today one agent reads last week's sales calls in ten minutes. Another turns what customers said into a landing page. Another launches thirty ads and kills the losers while you sleep. Another tells you on Monday which campaign brought in customers who paid. And the models are now good enough that if your idea is good, the output will be too.
A marketing engineer wires those agents into a machine. Part marketer, part builder. And the best ones often come from outside marketing: founders, engineers, operators, solo builders

https://t.co/vTTL7HprKo
hits.hook: Marketing Engineers: 100x More Experiments with AI agents  Marketing engineers are the new 10x employee, and most compan
hits.draft_en:
Greg's playbook in one line: one agent reads last week's sales calls in ten minutes, another turns them into a landing page, another launches thirty ads and kills the losers while you sleep.

100k views on 'marketing engineers'.

His advice is to build one agent and get it great before the second. Start with customer language: the exact words buyers use.

Export your last 20 sales call transcripts this weekend and have an agent pull the five phrases customers repeat most. Use the top one as your next headline.

hits.name: levelsio
hits.text:
Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night, not optimal

So I wanted to do the bathroom vent trick again, where putting the bathroom vent next to the bedroom on at night creates a low air pressure field and brings in new fresh air

But the light switch was tied to the vent here so it'd blast bright light into the bedroom if vent was on, so I closed it but then it didn't help a lot. So we split the light from the vent now and put it on and it worked!

About 600-700 ppm CO2 which is pretty great for indoors, outdoors is 400 for ex

Next house will have an ERV system built in but it'll be a lot of breaking ceilings and walls to put that into this one so this works for now

I use @airthings to measure the air quality in our house and bedroom, not affiliated, not paid but great brand and tip by @NorbertDragan
hits.hook: Update 2: We moved to a new bedroom and CO2 levels at night got very high again and we'd both regularly wake up at night
hits.quote_note: own May post: 100% sleep score with bathroom fan keeping CO2 low
hits.draft_en:
Pieter moved bedrooms and started waking up at night again. He did not guess why. He measured: CO2 was high.

He split the bathroom light from the vent, ran the vent at night, and got the room to about 600-700 ppm.

The fix was cheap. The meter is what made it possible.

Most builders tune their product on vibes. Put a meter on one thing users feel: load time, failed runs, time to first result.

Pick that one number today and log it for a week before you change anything.
hits.video_tip: 10s: air quality meter reading dropping from red to green, then a product dashboard metric doing the same, caption measure first, fix second.

hits.name: Alex Finn

You NEED to be running my 2 new favorite prompts for Grok Bot/Hark/Dots/Claude Code

Been getting so much more done with these

They're a morning/evening prompt I run first thing in the morning and right before I go to bed

Ben asked if people genuinely think code maintenance is not solvable with an agent. 39 replies.

outsiders.name: Theo - t3.gg
outsiders.text:
I got some issues with this.

The $132m/year is not real at all. Closer to $3m at today's prices, and as low as $1.2k within a year.

Yes, $132m -> $1.2k. Hear me out.

1. The price listed is not accurate at all.

$11m/month is just wrong. Real "api cost" is prolly $100k-$500k per month range.

The 1.5T tokens number includes cache'd tokens. I looked at my own usage, and 33.5B tokens came out to $0.56/m (under 1/10th of Peter's $8/m estimate).

I'm primarily using expensive models like Opus and Astra, and "1.5t tokens" would still have cost me ~$800k. If I used cheaper models and hit cache more, easily could get as low as $100k.

2. Intelligence is getting cheaper incredibly quickly

I know our LLM bills are going up and everyone is stressed about it. Totally reasonable! It's not because intelligence got more expensive.

Artificial Analysis tracks how "cost at a given intelligence level" drops over time. It used to drop at ~10x/year. Now it's at 30x lower in 5 months. (see image)

Assuming the $100k from before, cost could get as low as $3k/month in a few months, and if trends continue, $100/month by this time next year.

Obviously there will be smarter models and we will move to them, but replicating her experience today with equivalent models will be $1.2k/year by next year.

3. Nobody said this is normal

Lauren is the 0.0001% of "agentic engineer". Measuring her work as "$ in -> software out" is reductive and wrong.

Her spend should be looked at as a combination of product/eng, research, FDE work (pstack), and marketing. Worth $350k/day? No. Worth a mil or two a month? Absolutely.

She is exploring what happens when you ignore the cost of intelligence. She's not doing this because Cursor expects every company to spend $10m/year on tokens.

She's doing it because that $10m in tokens is going to cost $10,000 in a year or two.

Yohei called his approach a sillier method. It set a new cube packing record for n=12 at 2.931514578. 859k views.

Pieter ported DOOM multiplayer to the browser with Opus 5.5 in 30 minutes, bots in 10, and ran a LAN party for 10+ people with one URL.

An astrophysicist used Claude to build the first complete UV map of the sky in days instead of weeks.

None of these started as a roadmap item. They were weekend-sized bets on something nobody had bothered to try.

Pick one gap this weekend: a public benchmark, an engine with no web port, a dataset nobody combined. Give your agent 30 minutes and post the result either way.
